note: 3D terrain under the navigable channels (navigation_terrain.py). EU5 draws water as one plane at sea level and the terrain hides it wherever it is higher; the channels are sea tiles on a land heightmap, so they were invisible on the 3D terrain. One carve decal per vanilla heightmap tile that holds a channel, blend mode min: 1.0 (no effect) away from the channels, below the water level inside them. Heights are 0..1 of the world height (32 world units; water level = the game's NJominiMap water_level_percentage), distances in decal texels (half a location pixel) from the smoothed shore: inside the water falls by slope x d + curve x d^2 (centre of a 2-pixel channel ~0.6 world units deep, opaque), outside the bank rises gently (terrain at 0.15 meets it ~5 location pixels from the water). Decal names stay short (pp_channels_<k>_16): the constructor checks tracked paths against the Windows budget of 140 characters. Chosen 2026-10-03 on tile 5 (Rhine, Meuse, Scheldt) against vanilla's terrain mips: steepness p95 0.75 -> ~0.45, channel water kept at every mip.
